faqs.q: How much does a Neapolitan Mastiff cost to buy?
faqs.a: Reputable breeders typically charge $1,200–$4,000 for a Neapolitan Mastiff puppy. Prices vary by breeder reputation, health testing, and lineage. Rescue adoption fees are typically $100–$500 and include vaccinations, neutering, and microchipping.

faqs.q: What is the monthly cost of owning a Neapolitan Mastiff?
faqs.a: Budget $200–$400 per month for a Neapolitan Mastiff, covering food, preventive vet care, insurance, grooming and supplies. Large breeds cost more across every category — food portions, medication doses and professional services all scale with weight.

faqs.q: What are the biggest ongoing costs for a Neapolitan Mastiff?
faqs.a: The three largest annual expenses are food ($800–1,200), veterinary care ($400–$1,200 budgeted annually), and pet insurance ($800–1,800 per year). Grooming costs are lower for short-coated breeds managed at home.

faqs.q: How much does a Neapolitan Mastiff cost in the first year?
faqs.a: Year one costs for a Neapolitan Mastiff are significantly higher than subsequent years, typically $2,500–$5,000. This covers the purchase price or adoption fee, initial vet checks, vaccinations, spay/neuter, microchipping, crate, bedding, collar, leads and puppy training classes.

faqs.q: How often should I groom a Neapolitan Mastiff?
faqs.a: Neapolitan Mastiffs need brushing once or twice per week.  Nails should be trimmed every 3–4 weeks. Ears should be checked and cleaned monthly.

faqs.q: Do Neapolitan Mastiffs shed a lot?
faqs.a: Neapolitan Mastiffs have seasonal shedding — manageable with a consistent brushing routine.

faqs.q: What grooming tools does a Neapolitan Mastiff need?
faqs.a: A rubber grooming glove or soft-bristle brush is sufficient for weekly maintenance on the Neapolitan Mastiff's short coat. Add a nail grinder and ear cleaner for a complete grooming kit.

faqs.q: How often should I bathe a Neapolitan Mastiff?
faqs.a: Every 4–6 weeks is appropriate for most Neapolitan Mastiffs that live indoors. More frequent bathing is needed if they swim or spend time in mud. Over-bathing strips natural skin oils — use a pH-balanced dog shampoo rather than human products.

faqs.q: Are Neapolitan Mastiffs easy to train?
faqs.a: Neapolitan Mastiffs are moderately easy to train. They respond well to positive reinforcement and benefit from early puppy classes. Consistency from all household members is key.

faqs.q: What training method works best for a Neapolitan Mastiff?
faqs.a: Reward-based training using treats, praise and toy rewards is the most effective and well-researched approach for Neapolitan Mastiffs. Keep sessions short and positive, end on a success, and vary your rewards to maintain engagement.

faqs.q: At what age should I start training my Neapolitan Mastiff?
faqs.a: Start training from the day your puppy arrives home, typically at 8 weeks. The 8–16 week window is the most sensitive socialisation period. Enrol in a puppy class within the first two weeks for structured socialisation alongside basic obedience foundations.

faqs.q: How long does it take to train a Neapolitan Mastiff?
faqs.a: Most Neapolitan Mastiffs reliably perform basic cues within 4–6 weeks of daily 10–15 minute sessions. Reliable recall off-lead typically takes 3–4 months of progressive distance and distraction training.

faqs.q: What health problems do Neapolitan Mastiffs commonly have?
faqs.a: Neapolitan Mastiffs are most commonly associated with bloat (GDV). Regular vet checks, appropriate weight management, and breed-specific screening tests help detect issues early. Ask any breeder for health test results before purchasing.

faqs.q: How long do Neapolitan Mastiffs live?
faqs.a: Neapolitan Mastiffs have an average lifespan of 7–9 years. Larger breeds typically have shorter lifespans than smaller breeds. Maintaining a healthy weight and regular vet care are the most impactful factors for longevity.

faqs.q: Are Neapolitan Mastiffs prone to hip dysplasia?
faqs.a: Neapolitan Mastiffs have a moderate-to-elevated risk of hip dysplasia, particularly for large or active breeds. Ask for OFA or PennHIP hip evaluation certificates when buying from a breeder. Weight control and avoiding high-impact exercise during bone growth (under 18 months) reduces risk.

faqs.q: What health tests should a Neapolitan Mastiff puppy have?
faqs.a: At minimum, your Neapolitan Mastiff puppy should have a vet health check, first vaccinations, deworming, and microchipping before coming home. Ask the breeder for parent health certificates relevant to Neapolitan Mastiff-specific conditions. A vet check within 72 hours of bringing your puppy home is recommended to establish a baseline.

faqs.q: Are Neapolitan Mastiffs good with kids?
faqs.a: Neapolitan Mastiffs can be protective and may be cautious around unfamiliar children. Early socialisation with children from puppyhood significantly improves tolerance. Always supervise interactions between dogs and young children.

faqs.q: Do Neapolitan Mastiffs get along with other dogs?
faqs.a: Neapolitan Mastiffs can be selective with other dogs due to their protective nature. Early socialisation in puppy classes and controlled on-lead introductions with other dogs help build positive associations.

faqs.q: Do Neapolitan Mastiffs bark a lot?
faqs.a: Neapolitan Mastiffs tend to be vocal — they may bark at strangers, sounds, or when under-stimulated. Adequate daily exercise and mental enrichment (training sessions, puzzle feeders) significantly reduce nuisance barking. Teaching a "quiet" cue early is worthwhile.

faqs.q: Are Neapolitan Mastiffs good apartment dogs?
faqs.a: Neapolitan Mastiffs can live in apartments if their exercise needs are met consistently. The key variable is owner commitment to daily walks and enrichment — breed size alone doesn't determine apartment suitability.

faqs.q: How much exercise does a Neapolitan Mastiff need per day?
faqs.a: Neapolitan Mastiffs need approximately 45–60 minutes of exercise daily. A structured morning walk and an evening sniff walk usually cover their needs. Mental exercise (training sessions, puzzle feeders) counts toward overall stimulation needs and can reduce restless behaviour.

faqs.q: Are Neapolitan Mastiffs good running partners?
faqs.a: Neapolitan Mastiffs can join you for moderate runs once fully grown. They're better suited to steady 3–5 mile runs than extended distance. Watch for signs of fatigue and always run in cooler hours during summer.

faqs.q: What happens if a Neapolitan Mastiff doesn't get enough exercise?
faqs.a: Neapolitan Mastiffs are less demanding than high-energy breeds, but chronic under-exercise still leads to weight gain and low-level restlessness. Even lower-energy breeds benefit from a consistent daily walk for both physical health and mental stimulation.

faqs.q: Can a Neapolitan Mastiff be off-lead?
faqs.a: Neapolitan Mastiffs can be off-lead in secure areas once recall is reliable. Reliable recall typically takes 3–4 months of consistent training with progressive distance and distractions. Never trust off-lead recall in an unfenced area until it's been tested in controlled conditions first.

faqs.q: How much should I feed my Neapolitan Mastiff?
faqs.a: A Neapolitan Mastiff needs approximately 3–5 cups of dry food per day for an adult, split across two meals. Always follow the feeding guide on your specific formula — calorie density varies significantly between brands. Adjust portions based on body condition: you should be able to feel (but not easily see) the ribs.

faqs.q: How many times a day should I feed a Neapolitan Mastiff?
faqs.a: Adult Neapolitan Mastiffs should eat twice daily. Puppies (under 6 months) need 3–4 smaller meals per day to support growth and prevent hypoglycaemia, particularly in small breeds. For large and giant breeds, twice daily feeding also reduces the risk of bloat (GDV) compared to one large daily meal.

faqs.q: What is the best food for a Neapolitan Mastiff?
faqs.a: Look for a formula carrying an AAFCO adequacy statement for the correct life stage. A named protein source (chicken, turkey, beef, salmon) should appear first in the ingredient list. Medium-energy Neapolitan Mastiffs do well on standard adult maintenance formulas with named protein as the first ingredient.

faqs.q: When should I switch my Neapolitan Mastiff from puppy to adult food?
faqs.a: Large breeds should stay on a large-breed puppy formula until 18–24 months, then transition to an adult formula. Switching too early can disrupt joint development during the growth phase.

faqs.q: Is a Neapolitan Mastiff a good dog for first-time owners?
faqs.a: Neapolitan Mastiffs are manageable for motivated first-time owners who research the breed, commit to early training, and have realistic expectations about time and cost.

faqs.q: Are Neapolitan Mastiffs good family dogs?
faqs.a: Neapolitan Mastiffs can be good family dogs when properly socialised. Their suitability depends more on individual temperament and upbringing than breed alone.

faqs.q: Do Neapolitan Mastiffs do well when left alone?
faqs.a: Neapolitan Mastiffs form strong bonds with their owners and do not do well with extended isolation. Aim for no more than 4–6 hours alone at a time. If your schedule requires longer absences, consider a dog walker, doggy daycare, or a companion dog.

faqs.q: How much time do you need for a Neapolitan Mastiff?
faqs.a: Plan for 1.5–2 hours per day dedicated to your Neapolitan Mastiff — covering exercise, training, feeding and general interaction.  The commitment is consistent year-round, not just when convenient.
